items.title: ToolSmith: An Automatic Tool-Generation Framework for Multimodal Search Agents
items.snippet: Recent multimodal search agents use reasoning, vision, and live web search across many turns to answer questions beyond parametric knowledge by orchestrating a small library of hand-crafted search and visual tools. However, the library is laborious to create and maintain, and frozen when new query types, evidence formats, and failure modes are encountered in the wild. Human practitioners, by contrast, cope with insufficient tools by fashioning new ones from familiar parts and reusing them across tasks. Inspired by this, we propose ToolSmith, an automatic tool-generation framework that grows and reuses modules on top of a lean base tool library. We evaluate ToolSmith on three in-domain multim
items.title_ar: ToolSmith: توليد أدوات تلقائياً لوكلاء البحث متعددة الوسائط

items.why_en: It is useful if you build search agents that must handle new query types without constant manual tool maintenance.

items.title: LLMs Memorize Their Own Hallucinations During Post-Training
items.snippet: Reasoning domains have shaped the post-training recipes of frontier models even though they are trained and deployed in domains beyond math and code. In this paper, we study the consequences of directly adopting reasoning-centric training recipes, e.g., the use of outcome-based rewards for reinforcement learning (RL), injection of "cognitive" behaviors such as proposing and backtracking from hypotheses in reasoning chains, etc., for knowledge tasks. We hypothesize that these decisions, while useful for reasoning, inadvertently encourage models to memorize hallucinations they themselves generate in their long reasoning chains when trained on knowledge tasks. items.title_ar: LLMs تحفظ هلوساتها الخاصة أثناء post-training
items.summary_ar: تدرس الورقة تبعات تطبيق reasoning-centric training recipes، مثل outcome-based rewards في RL وإدخال سلوكيات cognitive، على المهام المعرفية. تفترض أن هذه الخيارات تشجع الموديلات على حفظ الهلاوس التي تولدها بنفسها في سلاسل التفكير الطويلة. تختبر الدراسة ذلك بتدريب موديلات على مهام معرفية لقياس هذا الحفظ.
items.why_ar: مهم جداً لأي فريق يعدّل LLMs للمهام المعرفية حيث تشكل الهلوسة خطراً في السياقات المالية والامتثالية.
items.title_en: LLMs Memorize Their Own Hallucinations During Post-Training
items.summary_en: The paper studies the consequences of applying reasoning-centric post-training recipes, such as outcome-based RL rewards and cognitive behaviors, to knowledge tasks. It hypothesizes that models memorize hallucinations they generate in long reasoning chains. The authors train models on knowledge tasks to measure this effect.
items.why_en: Directly relevant if you fine-tune LLMs for knowledge-heavy tasks where hallucination risk matters in financial contexts.

items.title: Wactorz: Self-Writing LLM Agents That Discover, Repair, and Migrate at the Edge
items.snippet: Most LLM agent frameworks build a crew that runs a task and exits. Physical environments (e.g., homes, labs, factory floors) need agents that stay up for months, survive their own bugs, and run on whatever hardware is already next to the sensors. We present Wactorz, an open-source runtime in which LLM-generated agents are long-lived, supervised actors: a planner turns a chat request into Python, compiles it into a new actor at runtime, and a supervisor restarts that actor alone, with its state intact, when it crashes. All coordination rides on MQTT, so agents can be spawned on, and live-migrated between, edge nodes such as a Raspberry Pi, and every internal event is a topic external systems
items.title_ar: Wactorz: وكلاء LLM ذاتية الكتابة تعمل طويلاً على الـ edge
items.summary_ar: يقدم Wactorz runtime مفتوح المصدر تُنشأ فيه agents بواسطة LLM كـ actors طويلة العمر ومراقَبة. يحوّل الـ planner طلب الدردشة إلى Python ويُترجمه إلى actor جديد في وقت التشغيل، ويعيد الـ supervisor تشغيل actor واحد مع حفظ حالته عند التعطل. تعتمد كل التنسيقات على MQTT، ويمكن نقل الـ agents بين عقد edge مثل Raspberry Pi.
items.why_ar: يمكن تجربته خلال أيام لاختبار أنماط الإشراف على agents تعمل باستمرار قرب الحساسات.
items.title_en: Wactorz: Self-Writing LLM Agents That Run Long-Lived at the Edge
items.summary_en: Wactorz is an open-source runtime where LLM-generated agents run as long-lived supervised actors. A planner turns a chat request into Python, compiles it into a new actor at runtime, and a supervisor restarts crashed actors with state intact. Coordination runs over MQTT, and agents can be spawned and live-migrated across edge nodes such as a Raspberry Pi.
items.why_en: It is an open-source runtime you can try within days to test long-running agent supervision patterns.

Here's a demo video, recorded on agent.datasette.io where you can sign in with GitHub to try the plugin yourself: Download the video (MP4) I prompt Datasette Agent to "Use #stats to show sqlite-utils downloads over time

items.title: datasette-agent 0.7a1
items.snippet: Release: datasette-agent 0.7a1 I small improvement to Datasette Agent : chat sessions can open an iframe side panel, and that panel can then navigate to different pages. This version improves navigation by fragment hashes, for deeper integration with other Datasette plugins that update fragment hashes when the user interacts with the plugin in a way that changes state. I built this in order to fix some bugs with the much more exciting datasette-charts 0.2a0 release . Tags: datasette-agent , data
items.title_ar: datasette-agent 0.7a1 يحسن التنقل عبر fragment hashes
items.summary_ar: تحديث صغير لـ Datasette Agent يتيح لجلسات الدردشة فتح لوحة جانبية بـ iframe والتنقل داخلها بين الصفحات. الإصدار يحسن التنقل اعتماداً على fragment hashes لدعم تكامل أعمق مع plugins أخرى تحدّث الـ hash عند تغيير الحالة، وقد أُنجز لإصلاح أخطاء في datasette-charts 0.2a0.

items.title_en: datasette-agent 0.7a1 improves navigation with fragment hashes
items.summary_en: A small update to Datasette Agent lets chat sessions open an iframe side panel that can navigate between pages. This version uses fragment hashes for navigation, enabling deeper integration with plugins that update hashes on state changes. It was built to fix bugs in the datasette-charts 0.2a0 release.
items.why_en: It is useful if you are building internal agent UIs that need shareable, state-aware navigation.
